subject.title: [Feature]: Add runtime testing for skill workshop proposals before apply

question: Should Skill Workshop gain a core pre-apply runtime validation command/action, and what sandbox, side-effect, skip, and override policy should govern candidate skill execution?
rationale: The missing capability is real, but executing proposed skill behavior before apply crosses a security and product boundary that code inspection cannot safely choose for maintainers.

options.title: Define a narrow core gate
options.body: Add load and schema checks first, then allow representative invocation only when maintainers define safe inputs, side-effect limits, and failure/override states.

options.title: Fold into lifecycle contract
options.body: Keep this as a subtask of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98002 and implement it only after the proposal health-report contract is settled.

options.title: Defer runtime invocation
options.body: Continue relying on static scanning and apply-time guards until Skill Workshop has a proven sandbox and health-report design.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow core gate
recommendation.body: Add load and schema checks first, then allow representative invocation only when maintainers define safe inputs, side-effect limits, and failure/override states.

likelyOwner.reason: The current Skill Workshop service/tool/CLI implementation in this checkout is routed through Peter Steinberger's recent carried commit, making him the best available owner signal for the boundary decision.
